summary: Jiro Sugiyama worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953), he held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1953–1988), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, Nagaoka University of Technology, and Bukkyo University.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendranath Mohanty was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1947–1949) and University of Göttingen (~1952–1954). He held posts at Calcutta (~1954–1967), Oklahoma (~1972–1986), and Temple University (~1986–2012).
Jitsuaki Oshika, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Tohoku University. He later held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jiyu Ren worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1934–1938), he served as director of the Institute of World Religions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2000).

Joachim Gentz specializes in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).
Joachim Prandstetter studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Vienna, completing his Magister by 1994 under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Leiden University. He held posts at Leipzig University (~1924–1935) and served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1945–1955).
Joan Halifax is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her studies at H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College (~1960–1964) and the University of Miami (~1968–1973).

Joanna Gottfried Williams worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969), she held posts at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1967 to 2022, serving as professor (~1967–2003).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology and studied at the University of Chicago (~1971–1976). She held posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (2002).

Joe Bransford Wilson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984), and held posts at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of London (~1967–1970), he served at the British Museum (1970–2010; attested 2013) and the Ashmolean Museum (~2011).
Joey Hung is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He held a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College.
Jogendra Singh studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Presidency University and Bangabasi College. He held lecturing posts at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog works in Buddhist, Iranian and Central Asian, and religious studies, earning a PhD from Indiana University (~1995–2000). He held posts at UC Santa Barbara (1997–1998) and Southern Methodist University (~2002).
Johann Andreas Schmeller was a linguistics scholar who held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1826–1852) and the Bavarian State Library (~1829–1852).
Johann Bernoulli worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Basel (~1757–1763), he was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (~1764–1807).
Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguistics scholar who studied at Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1752–1754).
